Share on X Telegram President Bola Tinubu on Saturday led a one-minute silence in honour of victims of the boat accident in Bayelsa State during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.
Tinubu also announced that Vice-President Kashim Shettima would visit the bereaved families and residents of Bayelsa State to convey the Federal Government’s condolences.
The President made the announcement while addressing party supporters at the rally, where he expressed sympathy with the people of Bayelsa over the tragedy.
He subsequently asked the audience to observe a minute of silence in memory of those who lost their lives.
“We show solidarity and sympathy; our condolences go to the people of Bayelsa State and the bereaved families. Can we have one minute silence?” he said.
Tinubu assured the affected families of the government’s support, adding that Shettima would undertake the condolence visit after the rally.
“We will support them. The Vice-President will go and condole with the families and the people of Bayelsa after this rally,” he added.
The boat accident occurred on Friday in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State when a vessel conveying mourners to a funeral capsized around Ukubie, near Oweikorogha community.
The Bayelsa State Police Command reported that four people died, while 24 others were rescued following the incident. Preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.
Following the tragedy, Tinubu had directed that the Ibadan presidential campaign rally be held without much fanfare as a mark of respect for the deceased and solidarity with their families.
He also directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to coordinate rescue and recovery operations.
